Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 49-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, foul-smelling urine, suprapubic pain, and mild hematuria—clinical picture most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis; empiric 3-day oral antibiotic prescribed.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “It hurts when I pee.”  
  – Onset 6 days ago; pain/burning on micturition.  
  – Foul urine odor, intermittent midline lower-abdominal pain (7/10, comes-and-goes), small “spots” of blood in urine.  
  – No fever/chills, flank/loin/back pain, nausea/vomiting, vaginal discharge, or prior similar episodes.  
• Pertinent negatives: denies recent dehydration, excessive exercise, sexual activity precipitant, change in bowel habit, weight loss.  
• PMH: Irritable bowel syndrome. No prior UTIs, renal disease, or surgeries reported.  
• Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg TID.  
• Allergies: Clindamycin (reaction details not specified).  
• Social / preventive: Lives with friends; support-worker occupation. Alcohol ~1 glass wine/week; non-smoker. No significant family history disclosed.

Examination:
• Virtual visit—no vitals or physical exam performed. No reported fever (does not own thermometer).

Impression:
• Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis (most likely).  
  – Supported by acute dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, microscopic hematuria, absence of systemic or flank signs.  
• Alternate considerations (less likely):  
  1. Urethritis secondary to STI—dysuria ± hematuria but patient denies precipitating sexual activity; no discharge.  
  2. Distal ureteric/bladder calculi—hematuria and pain possible, but colicky flank pain absent.

Plan:
• Pharmacologic: 3-day course of empiric oral antibiotic (prescription sent to Knightsbridge pharmacy; pick-up within 1 hr).  
• Supportive: Encourage ↑ oral fluids (2.5–3 L water/day); consider cranberry juice and OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets.  
• Monitoring: Purchase thermometer; check temperature periodically.  
• Safety-net: Seek medical review if pain worsens, develops fever ≥100.4 °F, flank/back pain, urinary retention, or symptoms persist/ recur.  
• Follow-up: No routine follow-up required if symptoms resolve; return if above red-flag symptoms or recurrent episodes.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: urinalysis/culture, vital signs, pregnancy status, exact antibiotic name/dose, detailed sexual history, reaction details to clindamycin, past gynecologic history.  
● Conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacks objective data (vitals, labs); some minor inaudible segments.
